subject: Default log capture — what stays by default (requests vs prompts vs generated outputs)
messages:
From: David Lopez <security@helixanalytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention specifics needed for vendor questionnaire

Hi Laura,

We're finishing our vendor security questionnaire for procurement and hit a few ambiguous items around log capture and retention for inference requests. Can you help clarify the default behavior for Redwood hosted API? Specifically: 

- Do you store the full request payload by default (we send prompts + metadata)?
- Are generated outputs retained by default, or only ephemeral?
- How do streaming responses affect storage (do streamed tokens get assembled and stored)?
- Is the KV/cache (session state) ever persisted as a log?
- What are the default retention windows and the deletion path if we ask for purge?

We need answers for the questionnaire by next Friday. I'm attaching the section of the questionnaire that references this. If possible, a short list of what customers can toggle (region, retention window, auto-purge) would be very helpful.

Thanks,
David Lopez
Security Lead
Helix Analytics

Attachment: helix_vendor_questionnaire_q4.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: David Lopez <security@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention specifics needed for vendor questionnaire

Hi David — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can paste into the questionnaire; I added exact field names and where customers can change settings in the Console. I attached our internal retention matrix for reference.

Short answers (defaults):
- Request payloads: by default we persist request metadata and the request body (prompts/inputs) for 45 days for hosted accounts. This enables billing/usage analytics and abuse monitoring.
- Generated outputs: generated model outputs are NOT stored long-term by default; we keep them transiently to satisfy in-flight request and short-term debugging (45-day retention only if the customer enables "retain outputs" or if the account is on a Dedicated/Private plan configured to persist outputs).
- Streaming: streamed tokens are assembled server-side for the in-flight response. Unless the customer enables output retention, the assembled output is treated per above (transient). We do keep some streaming telemetry (latency/byte counts) for 30 days for SLO telemetry only — not the token sequence.
- KV cache / session state: KV cache is ephemeral and never written to durable logs by default. It lives only in the serving layer for the lifetime of the session.
- Deletion/purge: customers can request an immediate purge via Console > Security > Data controls (self-service) or by opening a ticket. Purge initiation is typically acknowledged within 24–72 hours; tombstones are propagated across replicas and backups, and final residual removal can take up to 30 days in rare cases (see runbook).

What customers can toggle in Console: region residency (US/EU/APAC), default retention window (30/45/90/365 days), output-retention toggle (on/off), and auto-purge schedule. Dedicated and Private deployments can implement custom retention by contract.

Notes and exceptions:
- Legal hold / litigation or compliance investigations can override scheduled purges (we surface any holds to the customer).
- For EU-residency requests we can pin storage to an EU region; mandatory deletion requests are handled per regional laws and may have slightly different timelines due to cross-region replication.

I'll loop Markus for the technical purge timeline and the backup tombstone details. Let me know whether you want these answers in bullet form for the questionnaire or a one-page PDF.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-matrix-v2.xlsx (xlsx)

2) Confirm the deletion timeline: you said "acknowledged within 24–72 hours" — do you have an SLA or written runbook for the full removal timeline for backups/tombstones (we need a conservative timeline for procurement).

If you can confirm 1–3 in one short paragraph we can paste it directly into the questionnaire.

David — quick confirmations from the infra side to address the SLA/runbook asks: 

- Per-request opt-out: Yes. We support a per-request header x-redwood-no-store and a per-API-call parameter (store=false) that prevents request bodies/outputs from being written to durable logs. Note: the header must be present when the request arrives at our public API gateway; proxies or middleboxes should forward it unchanged.

- Streaming behavior: streamed tokens are buffered only in-memory to assemble the outgoing response. No assembled token sequences are persisted to long-term logs unless output-retention is explicitly enabled for the customer account. We do collect aggregate streaming telemetry (counts/latency), but that telemetry contains no token-level content.

- Deletion SLA/runbook: purge requests are triaged immediately. We acknowledge within 24 hours; purge initiation typically begins within 72 hours. Final irrevocable removal from primary stores and replicated caches usually completes within 7–30 days depending on backup retention and cross-region replication. Our conservative procurement-friendly statement is: "Initiate purge within 72 hours; complete final removal within 30 days in normal circumstances; legal holds may extend this." We'll provide that language in the questionnaire.

If you'd like, we can produce a signed statement for procurement (SOC2/controls reference) and a short one-page appendix describing the per-request header and Console location. Laura — happy to be the technical sign-off.

— Markus Klein
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
